finding.summary: `readStoredTheme` result is cast to `Theme` without validation; a junk stored value can throw from `classList.add`
finding.evidence: Line 65: `return (readStoredTheme(storageKey) as Theme) || defaultTheme;`. The new helper hardens the *access* but still returns any string unvalidated. A stored value containing whitespace (e.g. left by an older build, an extension, or a manual edit) flows into the effect at line 87 as `root.classList.add(theme)`, which throws `InvalidCharacterError` for a string with a space — an exception thrown from the provider's effect, i.e. the whole app. Any other junk value also silently mislabels `resolvedTheme` via the `theme as ResolvedTheme` cast at line 86. The sibling module added in this same change (`date-format-preference.ts`, `isFormat`) validates; this one does not.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. theme-provider.tsx:65 casts the raw localStorage string to Theme with only a falsy check (|| defaultTheme), so any non-empty junk value passes through. That value reaches theme-provider.tsx:87 root.classList.add(theme), which throws InvalidCharacterError for a token containing whitespace, from inside the provider effect that wraps the whole app (App.tsx:73); theme-provider.tsx:86 also mislabels resolvedTheme for any other junk value. No validation exists elsewhere for the vite-ui-theme key: the sole writer is writeStoredTheme (lines 33-40), which cannot constrain values left by older builds, extensions, or manual edits, and a grep of packages/frontend/src found no other guard. The URL path (line 64) and postMessage path (lines 118-120) are both validated, and the sibling module date-format-preference.ts:26-28,50-51 validates via isFormat, so no already-guarded ground applies. A missing-guard crash on an app-wide render path is squarely in the correctness lane.
